I farm in Quzhou, and there is really only one way to farm here that makes sense: winter wheat, then summer corn, same land, every year. My father did it, my neighbors do it, the whole county does it. The soil is flat, I have pump access to groundwater, and the flour mill and feed buyers both come to the village. I am not going to plant something I don't know just to be different.

I have 12 mu of contracted land. All of it goes into the wheat-corn rotation. Wheat is already in the ground from October — I will manage it through harvest in June, then turn right around and plant corn.

For wheat, I will top-dress urea at jointing stage in April, then irrigate twice more before harvest — once at jointing, once around heading. If I see aphids or rust in May I will spray, and I already sprayed herbicide in the fall. Yield around 450 jin per mu is what I expect. Anything over 500 is a good year.

For summer corn, I buy hybrid seed from the county seed shop — Zhengdan 958 or whatever my neighbor Lao Wang is buying, since that variety has been reliable. I plant directly into the stubble with the seeder right after wheat harvest, no plowing, to save time and moisture. I apply compound fertilizer at planting and top-dress urea at the bell stage. If July and August are dry, I pump once. I spray herbicide right after emergence and watch for armyworm later in the season.

I apply plenty of fertilizer — I know the extension station says I use too much nitrogen, but I would rather have a heavier hand and not lose the crop than be cautious and come up short.
